sanskrit: dilīpas tu tataḥ śrutvā pitṝṇāṃ nidhanaṃ mahat paryatapyata duḥkhena teṣāṃ gatim acintayat
english: Then Dilīpa, upon hearing of the great destruction of his ancestors, was tormented by grief and pondered on their fate.

sanskrit: gaṅgāvataraṇe yatnaṃ sumahac cākaron nṛpaḥ na cāvatārayām āsa ceṣṭamāno yathābalam
english: The king made an immense effort to bring down the Gaṅgā, but try as he might with all his strength, he could not cause her to descend.

sanskrit: tasya putraḥ samabhavac chrīmān dharmaparāyaṇaḥ bhagīratha iti khyātaḥ satyavāg anasūyakaḥ
english: His son was born — glorious, devoted to righteousness, known as Bhagīratha, truthful in speech and free from envy.

sanskrit: abhiṣicya tu taṃ rājye dilīpo vanam āśritaḥ tapaḥsiddhisamāyogāt sa rājā bharatarṣabha vanāj jagāma tridivaṃ kālayogena bhārata
english: Having consecrated him in the kingdom, Dilīpa retired to the forest; and that king, O bull of the Bhāratas, in time attained the perfection of austerity and departed from the forest to heaven.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca sa tu rājā maheṣvāsaś cakravartī mahārathaḥ babhūva sarvalokasya manonayananandanaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: That king, a great archer, a wheel-turner of empire, a mighty chariot-warrior, became the delight of the hearts and eyes of all the worlds.

sanskrit: sa śuśrāva mahābāhuḥ kapilena mahātmanā pitṝṇāṃ nidhanaṃ ghoram aprāptiṃ tridivasya ca
english: The mighty-armed one heard of the terrible destruction of his ancestors by the great-souled Kapila and of their failure to attain heaven.

sanskrit: sa rājyaṃ sacive nyasya hṛdayena vidūyatā jagāma himavatpārśvaṃ tapas taptuṃ nareśvaraḥ
english: He, the lord of men, entrusted the kingdom to his ministers with a heart torn by sorrow, and went to the slopes of the Himālayas to perform austerities.

sanskrit: ārirādhayiṣur gaṅgāṃ tapasā dagdhakilbiṣaḥ so 'paśyata naraśreṣṭha himavantaṃ nagottamam
english: Wishing to propitiate the Gaṅgā and having burned away his sins through austerity, he, best of men, beheld Himavat, the greatest of mountains.

sanskrit: śṛṅgair bahuvidhākārair dhātumadbhir alaṃkṛtam pavanālambibhir meghaiḥ pariṣvaktaṃ samantataḥ
english: It was adorned with peaks of many varied forms rich in minerals, and embraced on all sides by clouds that clung to the winds.

sanskrit: nadīkuñjanitambaiś ca sodakair upaśobhitam guhākandarasaṃlīnaiḥ siṃhavyāghrair niṣevitam
english: It was beautified by river-thickets and water-bearing slopes, and frequented by lions and tigers lurking in caves and ravines.

sanskrit: śakunaiś ca vicitrāṅgaiḥ kūjadbhir vividhā giraḥ bhṛṅgarājais tathā haṃsair dātyūhair jalakukkuṭaiḥ
english: It rang with the varied calls of vividly coloured birds — with the songs of the bhṛṅgarāja, the haṃsa, the dātyūha, and the water-hen.

sanskrit: mayūraiḥ śatapatraiś ca kokilair jīvajīvakaiḥ cakorair asitāpāṅgais tathā putrapriyair api
english: It resounded with peacocks, lotus-birds, cuckoos, jīvajīvaka birds, dark-eyed cakor partridges, and also the birds called putrapriya.

sanskrit: jalasthāneṣu ramyeṣu padminībhiś ca saṃkulam sārasānāṃ ca madhurair vyāhṛtaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam
english: Its lovely water-places were crowded with lotus-groves, and it was adorned by the sweet cries of sārasa cranes.

sanskrit: kiṃnarair apsarobhiś ca niṣevitaśilātalam diśāgajaviṣāṇāgraiḥ samantād ghṛṣṭapādapam
english: Its rocky surfaces were frequented by kiṃnaras and apsarases, and its trees were rubbed on all sides by the tusk-tips of the elephants of the quarters.

sanskrit: vidyādharānucaritaṃ nānāratnasamākulam viṣolbaṇair bhujaṃgaiś ca dīptajihvair niṣevitam
english: It was roamed by vidyādharas, teeming with gems of every kind, and haunted by venomous serpents with flaming tongues.

sanskrit: kva cit kanakasaṃkāśaṃ kva cid rajatasaṃnibham kva cid añjanapuñjābhaṃ himavantam upāgamat
english: He approached Himavat — golden in some places, silver-white in others, resembling heaps of collyrium in yet others.

sanskrit: sa tu tatra naraśreṣṭhas tapo ghoraṃ samāśritaḥ phalamūlāmbubhakṣo 'bhūt sahasraṃ parivatsarān
english: There that best of men embraced fierce austerity, subsisting on fruits, roots, and water for a thousand years.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarasahasre tu gate divye mahānadī darśayām āsa taṃ gaṅgā tadā mūrtimatī svayam
english: When a thousand years had passed, the divine great river Gaṅgā revealed herself to him in embodied form.

sanskrit: gaṅgovāca kim icchasi mahārāja mattaḥ kiṃ ca dadāni te tad bravīhi naraśreṣṭha kariṣyāmi vacas tava
english: The Gaṅgā said: What do you desire from me, great king, and what shall I give you? Speak, best of men — I will fulfil your word.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca rājā haimavatīṃ tadā pitāmahā me varade kapilena mahānadi anveṣamāṇās turagaṃ nītā vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Lomaśa said: Thus addressed, the king replied to the daughter of Himavat then: 'O boon-giving great river, my grandsires, while searching for the horse, were carried off to the abode of Vaivasvata by Kapila.'

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭis tāni sahasrāṇi sāgarāṇāṃ mahātmanām kāpilaṃ teja āsādya kṣaṇena nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: 'Those sixty thousand great-souled sons of Sagara, encountering the fire of Kapila, perished in an instant.'

sanskrit: teṣām evaṃ vinaṣṭānāṃ svarge vāso na vidyate yāvat tāni śarīrāṇi tvaṃ jalair nābhiṣiñcasi
english: 'For those thus destroyed, there is no dwelling in heaven so long as you do not sprinkle their bodies with your waters.'

sanskrit: svargaṃ naya mahābhāge matpitṝn sagarātmajān teṣām arthe 'bhiyācāmi tvām ahaṃ vai mahānadi
english: 'O most blessed one, convey my ancestors, the sons of Sagara, to heaven — for their sake I implore you, O great river.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco rājño gaṅgā lokanamaskṛtā bhagīratham idaṃ vākyaṃ suprītā samabhāṣata
english: Hearing the king's words, the Gaṅgā, worshipped by all worlds, was greatly pleased and spoke these words to Bhagīratha.

sanskrit: kariṣyāmi mahārāja vacas te nātra saṃśayaḥ vegaṃ tu mama durdhāryaṃ patantyā gaganāc cyutam
english: 'I will fulfil your word, great king — there is no doubt of this. But my current as I fall, discharged from the sky, is hard to bear.'

sanskrit: na śaktas triṣu lokeṣu kaś cid dhārayituṃ nṛpa anyatra vibudhaśreṣṭhān nīlakaṇṭhān maheśvarāt
english: 'No one in the three worlds is able to hold me, O king, except the best of the immortals, the blue-throated Maheśvara.'

sanskrit: taṃ toṣaya mahābāho tapasā varadaṃ haram sa tu māṃ pracyutāṃ devaḥ śirasā dhārayiṣyati kariṣyati ca te kāmaṃ pitṝṇāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: 'Propitiate him, O mighty-armed one, Hara the boon-giver, through austerity; that god will bear me on his head as I descend, and will fulfil your wish out of desire for the welfare of your ancestors.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco rājan mahārājo bhagīrathaḥ kailāsaṃ parvataṃ gatvā toṣayām āsa śaṃkaram
english: Hearing these words, O king, great king Bhagīratha went to Mount Kailāsa and pleased Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: tatas tena samāgamya kālayogena kena cit agṛhṇāc ca varaṃ tasmād gaṅgāyā dhāraṇaṃ nṛpa svargavāsaṃ samuddiśya pitṝṇāṃ sa narottamaḥ
english: Then, having met with him after some time had passed, that best of men received from him the boon of bearing the Gaṅgā, O king, with the aim of securing heaven for his ancestors.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca bhagīrathavacaḥ śrutvā priyārthaṃ ca divaukasām evam astv iti rājānaṃ bhagavān pratyabhāṣata
english: Lomaśa said: Hearing the words of Bhagīratha and for the benefit of the gods as well, the Blessed Lord replied to the king: 'So be it.'

sanskrit: dhārayiṣye mahābāho gaganāt pracyutāṃ śivām divyāṃ devanadīṃ puṇyāṃ tvatkṛte nṛpasattama
english: 'I will bear the auspicious divine holy river of the gods as she falls from the sky — for your sake, best of kings, O mighty-armed one.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāho himavantam upāgamat saṃvṛtaḥ pārṣadair ghorair nānāpraharaṇodyataiḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed one approached Himavat, surrounded by terrible attendants brandishing various weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ sthitvā naraśreṣṭhaṃ bhagīratham uvāca ha prayācasva mahābāho śailarājasutāṃ nadīm patamānāṃ saricchreṣṭhāṃ dhārayiṣye triviṣṭapāt
english: Then, having stationed himself there, he said to Bhagīratha, best of men: 'O mighty-armed one, pray to the daughter of the mountain-king — I shall bear the best of rivers as she falls from heaven.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco rājā śarveṇa samudāhṛtam prayataḥ praṇato bhūtvā gaṅgāṃ samanucintayat
english: Hearing the words spoken by Śarva, the king, purified and bowing in reverence, meditated upon the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṇyajalā ramyā rājñā samanucintitā īśānaṃ ca sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā gaganāt sahasā cyutā
english: Then the lovely, pure-watered river, thought upon by the king and seeing Īśāna standing ready, suddenly fell from the sky.

sanskrit: tāṃ pracyutāṃ tato dṛṣṭvā devāḥ sārdhaṃ maharṣibhiḥ gandharvoragarakṣāṃsi samājagmur didṛkṣayā
english: Seeing her fall, the gods together with the great sages, along with gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas, came together to witness the sight.

sanskrit: tataḥ papāta gaganād gaṅgā himavataḥ sutā samudbhrāntamahāvartā mīnagrāhasamākulā
english: Then the Gaṅgā, daughter of Himavat, fell from the sky with her great eddies swirling wildly, teeming with fish and crocodiles.

sanskrit: tāṃ dadhāra haro rājan gaṅgāṃ gaganamekhalām lalāṭadeśe patitāṃ mālāṃ muktāmayīm iva
english: Hara received her, O king — the Gaṅgā, girdled by the sky — as she fell upon his forehead, like a garland of pearls.

sanskrit: sā babhūva visarpantī tridhā rājan samudragā phenapuñjākulajalā haṃsānām iva paṅktayaḥ
english: She spread out, O king, flowing in three streams to the ocean, her waters thick with masses of foam, like rows of swans.

sanskrit: kva cid ābhogakuṭilā praskhalantī kva cit kva cit svaphenapaṭasaṃvītā matteva pramadāvrajat kva cit sā toyaninadair nadantī nādam uttamam
english: Somewhere she wound in sweeping curves, somewhere she leapt and stumbled, wrapped in her own veil of foam she moved like an ecstatic woman; somewhere she roared with the great sound of rushing waters.

sanskrit: evaṃ prakārān subahūn kurvantī gaganāc cyutā pṛthivītalam āsādya bhagīratham athābravīt
english: Performing many such displays as she fell from the sky and reached the surface of the earth, she then spoke to Bhagīratha.

sanskrit: darśayasva mahārāja mārgaṃ kena vrajāmy aham tvadartham avatīrṇāsmi pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpate
english: 'Show me the way, great king — where shall I go? It is for your sake, O lord of the earth, that I have descended to the earth.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco rājā prātiṣṭhata bhagīrathaḥ yatra tāni śarīrāṇi sāgarāṇāṃ mahātmanām pāvanārthaṃ naraśreṣṭha puṇyena salilena ha
english: Hearing these words, King Bhagīratha set out toward where the bodies of those great-souled sons of Sagara lay, so that they might be purified, O best of men, by the sacred waters.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyā dhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā haro lokanamaskṛtaḥ kailāsaṃ parvataśreṣṭhaṃ jagāma tridaśaiḥ saha
english: Having borne the Gaṅgā, Hara, worshipped by all worlds, departed to Kailāsa, best of mountains, together with the gods.

sanskrit: samudraṃ ca samāsādya gaṅgayā sahito nṛpaḥ pūrayām āsa vegena samudraṃ varuṇālayam
english: Reaching the ocean together with the Gaṅgā, the king filled with her rushing current the ocean, the abode of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: duhitṛtve ca nṛpatir gaṅgāṃ samanukalpayat pitṝṇāṃ codakaṃ tatra dadau pūrṇamanorathaḥ
english: The king adopted the Gaṅgā as a daughter, and there, his heart's desire fulfilled, he performed the water-offering for his ancestors.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ gaṅgā tripathagā yathā pūraṇārthaṃ samudrasya pṛthivīm avatāritā
english: I have told you everything — how the Gaṅgā, flowing through three paths, was brought down to earth for the filling of the ocean.

sanskrit: samudraś ca yathā pītaḥ kāraṇārthe mahātmanā vātāpiś ca yathā nītaḥ kṣayaṃ sa brahmahā prabho agastyena mahārāja yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: And how the ocean was drunk by that great-souled one for a purpose, and how Vātāpi, that slayer of brahmins, was brought to destruction by Agastya, O great king — this is what you asked me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prayātaḥ kaunteyaḥ krameṇa bharatarṣabha nandām aparanandāṃ ca nadyau pāpabhayāpahe
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the son of Kuntī journeyed onward, O bull of the Bhāratas, and came in succession to the rivers Nandā and Aparanandā, which dispel the fear of sin.

sanskrit: sa parvataṃ samāsādya hemakūṭam anāmayam acintyān adbhutān bhāvān dadarśa subahūn nṛpaḥ
english: Approaching the salubrious mountain Hemakūṭa, the king beheld very many inconceivable and wondrous phenomena.

sanskrit: vāco yatrābhavan meghā upalāś ca sahasraśaḥ nāśaknuvaṃs tam āroḍhuṃ viṣaṇṇamanaso janāḥ
english: There, where sounds became clouds and thousands of stones rained down, people with despondent minds could not climb it.

sanskrit: vāyur nityaṃ vavau yatra nityaṃ devaś ca varṣati sāyaṃ prātaś ca bhagavān dṛśyate havyavāhanaḥ
english: The wind always blew there, rain always fell there, and morning and evening the blessed fire-carrier was to be seen.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhān bhāvān adbhutān vīkṣya pāṇḍavaḥ lomaśaṃ punar eva sma paryapṛcchat tad adbhutam
english: Having observed these many wondrous phenomena, the Pāṇḍava then questioned Lomaśa again about those marvels.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca yathāśrutam idaṃ pūrvam asmābhir arikarśana tad ekāgramanā rājan nibodha gadato mama
english: Lomaśa said: As I have heard it of old, O destroyer of foes, hear it from me now with focused mind, O king.

sanskrit: asminn ṛṣabhakūṭe 'bhūd ṛṣabho nāma tāpasaḥ anekaśatavarṣāyus tapasvī kopano bhṛśam
english: On this Ṛṣabhakūṭa there lived an ascetic named Ṛṣabha, who lived for many hundreds of years — a man of austerity and exceedingly wrathful.

sanskrit: sa vai saṃbhāṣyamāṇo 'nyaiḥ kopād girim uvāca ha ya iha vyāharet kaś cid upalān utsṛjes tadā
english: Once, when addressed by others, he declared in anger to the mountain: 'Whoever speaks here shall rain down stones.'

sanskrit: vātaṃ cāhūya mā śabdam ity uvāca sa tāpasaḥ vyāharaṃś caiva puruṣo meghena vinivāryate
english: Summoning the wind, that ascetic declared: 'Let there be no noise!' — and indeed, whoever speaks is blocked by a cloud.

sanskrit: evam etāni karmāṇi rājaṃs tena maharṣiṇā kṛtāni kāni cit kopāt pratiṣiddhāni kāni cit
english: Thus, O king, these phenomena were set in motion by that great seer — some out of anger, others as prohibitions.

sanskrit: nandām abhigatān devān purā rājann iti śrutiḥ anvapadyanta sahasā puruṣā devadarśinaḥ
english: It is heard, O king, that long ago, men who were seers of the gods suddenly followed after the gods who had come to Nandā.

sanskrit: te darśanam anicchanto devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ durgaṃ cakrur imaṃ deśaṃ giripratyūharūpakam
english: Not wishing to be seen, the gods led by Śakra made this region impassable, in the form of a mountain barrier.

sanskrit: tadā prabhṛti kaunteya narā girim imaṃ sadā nāśaknuvan abhidraṣṭuṃ kuta evādhirohitum
english: From that time onward, O son of Kuntī, men were never able to even see this mountain, let alone climb it.

sanskrit: nātaptatapasā śakyo draṣṭum eṣa mahāgiriḥ āroḍhuṃ vāpi kaunteya tasmān niyatavāg bhava
english: This great mountain cannot be seen or climbed by one who has not heated himself with austerity, O son of Kuntī — therefore keep your speech restrained.

sanskrit: iha devāḥ sadā sarve yajñān ājahrur uttamān teṣām etāni liṅgāni dṛśyante 'dyāpi bhārata
english: Here all the gods have always conducted supreme sacrifices, and the marks of those sacrifices are visible even today, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kuśākāreva dūrveyaṃ saṃstīrṇeva ca bhūr iyam yūpaprakārā bahavo vṛkṣāś ceme viśāṃ pate
english: This grass resembles kuśa, this ground appears as if strewn with sacred grass, and these many trees stand like sacrificial posts, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: devāś ca ṛṣayaś caiva vasanty adyāpi bhārata teṣāṃ sāyaṃ tathā prātar dṛśyate havyavāhanaḥ
english: Gods and sages still dwell here even today, O Bhārata, and their fire-bearer is to be seen at evening and at morning.

sanskrit: ihāplutānāṃ kaunteya sadyaḥ pāpmā vihanyate kuruśreṣṭhābhiṣekaṃ vai tasmāt kuru sahānujaḥ
english: For those who bathe here, O son of Kuntī, sin is immediately destroyed. Therefore, O best of the Kurus, perform ablution together with your brothers.

sanskrit: tato nandāplutāṅgas tvaṃ kauśikīm abhiyāsyasi viśvāmitreṇa yatrograṃ tapas taptam anuttamam
english: Then, with limbs purified by bathing in the Nandā, you will proceed to the Kauśikī, where Viśvāmitra performed his fierce and unsurpassed austerity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tatra samāplutya gātrāṇi sagaṇo nṛpaḥ jagāma kauśikīṃ puṇyāṃ ramyāṃ śivajalāṃ nadīm
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having bathed there, the king with his retinue set off toward the Kauśikī — the holy, lovely river with auspicious waters.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca eṣā devanadī puṇyā kauśikī bharatarṣabha viśvāmitrāśramo ramya eṣa cātra prakāśate
english: Lomaśa said: This is the holy river of the gods, the Kauśikī, O bull of the Bhāratas, and here shines forth the lovely hermitage of Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: āśramaś caiva puṇyākhyaḥ kāśyapasya mahātmanaḥ ṛśyaśṛṅgaḥ suto yasya tapasvī saṃyatendriyaḥ
english: Here too is the hermitage known as holy, that of the great-souled Kāśyapa, whose son was the ascetic Ṛśyaśṛṅga, master of his senses.

sanskrit: tapaso yaḥ prabhāvena varṣayām āsa vāsavam anāvṛṣṭyāṃ bhayād yasya vavarṣa balavṛtrahā
english: He who by the power of his austerity caused Vāsava to send rain, and out of fear of whom the mighty slayer of Vṛtra rained during a drought.

sanskrit: mṛgyāṃ jātaḥ sa tejasvī kāśyapasya sutaḥ prabhuḥ viṣaye lomapādasya yaś cakārādbhutaṃ mahat
english: That radiant, mighty son of Kāśyapa was born of a doe, and in the kingdom of Lomapāda he performed a great wonder.

sanskrit: nivartiteṣu sasyeṣu yasmai śāntāṃ dadau nṛpaḥ lomapādo duhitaraṃ sāvitrīṃ savitā yathā
english: When the crops had been restored, the king Lomapāda gave him Śāntā as his daughter, just as Savitṛ gave Sāvitrī.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ṛśyaśṛṅgaḥ kathaṃ mṛgyām utpannaḥ kāśyapātmajaḥ viruddhe yonisaṃsarge kathaṃ ca tapasā yutaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was Ṛśyaśṛṅga, the son of Kāśyapa, born of a doe through a union contrary to nature, and how did he come to be endowed with austerity?

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ ca bhayāc chakras tasya bālasya dhīmataḥ anāvṛṣṭyāṃ pravṛttāyāṃ vavarṣa balavṛtrahā
english: And why, when drought had set in, did the mighty Śakra, slayer of Vṛtra, rain out of fear of that wise boy?

sanskrit: kathaṃrūpā ca śāntābhūd rājaputrī yatavratā lobhayām āsa yā ceto mṛgabhūtasya tasya vai
english: And what manner of woman was Śāntā, the king's daughter, strict in her vow, who captivated the heart of that one who had been as a deer?

sanskrit: lomapādaś ca rājarṣir yadāśrūyata dhārmikaḥ kathaṃ vai viṣaye tasya nāvarṣat pākaśāsanaḥ
english: And Lomapāda, the royal sage heard of as righteous — how was it that in his kingdom Pākaśāsana did not rain?

sanskrit: etan me bhagavan sarvaṃ vistareṇa yathātatham vaktum arhasi śuśrūṣor ṛṣyaśṛṅgasya ceṣṭitam
english: All this, O blessed one, you should tell me in full and as it truly happened — I am eager to hear of the deeds of Ṛśyaśṛṅga.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca vibhāṇḍakasya brahmarṣes tapasā bhāvitātmanaḥ amoghavīryasya sataḥ prajāpatisamadyuteḥ
english: Lomaśa said: Of Vibhāṇḍaka the brahmin-seer, whose self was refined by austerity, whose virility was infallible, who was righteous and of splendour equal to Prajāpati —

sanskrit: śṛṇu putro yathā jāta ṛśyaśṛṅgaḥ pratāpavān mahāhrade mahātejā bālaḥ sthavirasaṃmataḥ
english: — hear how was born his son Ṛśyaśṛṅga of great valour, greatly radiant, a boy esteemed by the elders, born in a great lake.
